OR Art. 76 Abs. 1.summary: If a time is set for the beginning or the end of a month, this means the first or the last day of that month.
OR Art. 76 Abs. 1.draft: If a time is set to begin or end on the first or last day of a month, that day is the first or last day of that month.
OR Art. 76 Abs. 1.change_note: Draft was circular ('set to begin or end on the first or last day ... is the first or last day').

OR Art. 76 Abs. 2.summary: If a time is set for the middle of a month, the fifteenth day of that month applies.
OR Art. 76 Abs. 2.draft: If a time is set for the middle of a month, the fifteenth day of that month applies.

OR Art. 77 Abs. 1.summary: If an obligation is to be performed (or another legal act done) when a set period after the contract was concluded expires, the date is: 1. for a period in days, the last day of the period, not counting the day the contract was concluded; a period of 8 or 15 days means a full 8 or 15 days, not one or two weeks; 2. for a period in weeks, the day of the last week with the same weekday name as the day the contract was concluded; 3. for a period in months or a multi-month period (year, half-year, quarter), the day of the last month with the same date number as the day the contract was concluded, or the last day of that month if it has no such date. A 'half month' counts as 15 days, counted last when a period is stated as one or more months and a half.
OR Art. 77 Abs. 1.draft: If a contractual obligation or legal act is to occur after a specific time limit following the contract's conclusion, the deadline falls: 1. if the period is measured in days, on the last day of that period, excluding the day the contract was signed, and if the period is eight or 15 days, it means exactly eight or 15 full days rather than one or two weeks; 2. if the period is measured in weeks, on the day of the final week that corresponds in name to the day the contract was signed; 3. if the period is measured in months or a multi-month period (year, half-year, quarter-year), on the day of the final month that corresponds in number to the day the contract was signed, and if that day does not exist in the final month, on the last day of that month. The term "half-month" is equivalent to a 15-day period, which is counted last if a deadline includes one or more months plus a half-month.
OR Art. 77 Abs. 1.change_note: 'Signed' replaced by 'concluded' (the text speaks of conclusion, not signature); wording tightened.

OR Art. 77 Abs. 2.summary: The time limit is calculated in the same way if it begins to run not from the day the contract is concluded, but from another specified point in time.
OR Art. 77 Abs. 2.draft: The time limit is calculated in the same way if it begins to run not from the day the contract is concluded, but from another specified point in time.

OR Art. 77 Abs. 3.summary: If performance must occur within a specific deadline, it must be completed before that deadline expires.
OR Art. 77 Abs. 3.draft: If performance must occur within a specific deadline, it must be completed before that deadline expires.

OR Art. 78 Abs. 1.summary: If the due date or the last day of a deadline falls on a Sunday or another public holiday recognized by the state at the place of performance, the next working day is considered the due date or the last day of the deadline.
OR Art. 78 Abs. 1.draft: If the due date or the last day of a deadline falls on a Sunday or another public holiday recognized by the state at the place of performance, the next working day is considered the due date or the last day of the deadline.

OR Art. 78 Abs. 2.change_note: Draft 'No alternative agreements are excluded' was garbled; the text reserves different agreements.

OR Art. 97 Abs. 1.summary: If an obligation is not performed at all or not properly, the debtor must pay compensation for the resulting damage unless they prove that they were not at fault in any way.
OR Art. 97 Abs. 1.draft: If a debtor cannot fulfill an obligation at all or properly, they must compensate for any resulting damage, unless they prove no fault of their own is attributable to them.
OR Art. 97 Abs. 1.change_note: Draft said the debtor 'cannot fulfil'; the text covers any non-performance or improper performance.

OR Art. 97 Abs. 2.summary: Enforcement is governed by the Federal Act of 11 April 1889 on Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy and the Civil Procedure Code of 19 December 2008 (ZPO).
OR Art. 97 Abs. 2.draft: For enforcement, the provisions of the Federal Act of 11 April 1889 on Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy and the Civil Procedure Act of 19 December 2008 apply.
OR Art. 97 Abs. 2.change_note: Name of the ZPO corrected ('Civil Procedure Code', abbreviation added).

OR Art. 143 Abs. 1.summary: Several debtors become jointly and severally liable when they declare that each of them will be individually liable to the creditor for the whole debt.
OR Art. 143 Abs. 1.draft: Solidarity among multiple debtors arises only if each debtor declares that they will be individually liable to the creditor for the entire debt. This declaration must be made by each debtor to the creditor.
OR Art. 143 Abs. 1.change_note: Removed an added sentence and the added word 'only'; named the concept (joint and several liability).

OR Art. 143 Abs. 2.summary: Without such a declaration, joint and several liability arises only in cases set by law.
OR Art. 143 Abs. 2.draft: Without such a declaration of intent, solidarity arises only in the cases prescribed by law.
OR Art. 143 Abs. 2.change_note: Terminology aligned ('solidarity' -> joint and several liability).

OR Art. 144 Abs. 1.summary: The creditor may choose to demand the whole debt, or only part of it, from each of the jointly and severally liable debtors.
OR Art. 144 Abs. 1.draft: The creditor may demand either a portion or the entire amount from any one of the joint debtors. This right applies to all joint debtors collectively.
OR Art. 144 Abs. 1.change_note: Removed an added sentence that was confusing ('applies to all joint debtors collectively').

OR Art. 144 Abs. 2.summary: All the debtors remain bound until the whole claim has been paid.
OR Art. 144 Abs. 2.draft: All debtors remain obligated until the entire claim is settled. This obligation applies to all debtors, including spouses or registered partners, and continues until the full amount of the claim is paid.
OR Art. 144 Abs. 2.change_note: Removed invented reference to spouses or registered partners.

OR Art. 148 Abs. 1.summary: If the legal relationship among the joint debtors does not provide otherwise, each joint debtor must assume an equal share of any payment made to the creditor.
OR Art. 148 Abs. 1.draft: If the legal relationship among the joint debtors does not provide otherwise, each joint debtor must assume an equal share of any payment made to the creditor.

OR Art. 148 Abs. 2.summary: If a joint debtor pays more than their share, they are entitled to claim reimbursement for the excess amount from the other joint debtors.
OR Art. 148 Abs. 2.draft: If a joint debtor pays more than their share, they are entitled to claim reimbursement for the excess amount from the other joint debtors.

OR Art. 148 Abs. 3.summary: If a co-debtor cannot provide their share, the remaining co-debtors must each bear an equal portion of that unobtainable amount.
OR Art. 148 Abs. 3.draft: If a co-debtor cannot provide their share, the remaining co-debtors must each bear an equal portion of that unobtainable amount.

OR Art. 253.summary: Through a rental contract, the landlord commits to letting the tenant use a thing, and the tenant commits to paying the landlord rent for it.
OR Art. 253.draft: Through a rental contract, the landlord commits to letting the tenant use a thing, and the tenant commits to paying the landlord rent for it.

OR Art. 253a Abs. 1.summary: The rules on renting residential and business premises also apply to things that the landlord lets the tenant use together with those premises.
OR Art. 253a Abs. 1.draft: The provisions on renting residential and business premises also apply to items that the landlord provides to the tenant for use together with those premises. This applies only to items that the landlord provides to the tenant for use together with the residential or business premises.

OR Art. 253a Abs. 2.summary: The rules on renting residential and business premises do not apply to holiday homes rented for three months or less.
OR Art. 253a Abs. 2.draft: They do not apply to holiday homes rented for a maximum of three months.
OR Art. 253a Abs. 2.change_note: 'They' replaced by what it refers to, so the summary stands alone.

OR Art. 253a Abs. 3.summary: The Federal Council issues the implementing regulations.
OR Art. 253a Abs. 3.draft: The Federal Council issues the implementing regulations.

OR Art. 253b Abs. 1.summary: The provisions on protection against abusive rents (Art. 269 ff.) apply by analogy to non-agricultural lease and other contracts that essentially govern the letting of residential or business premises for remuneration.
OR Art. 253b Abs. 1.draft: The provisions on protection against abusive rents (Art. 269 ff.) apply by analogy to non-agricultural lease and other contracts that essentially govern the letting of residential or business premises for remuneration.

OR Art. 253b Abs. 2.summary: The rules protecting against abusive rents do not apply to the rental of luxury flats and single-family houses with six or more living rooms (not counting the kitchen).
OR Art. 253b Abs. 2.draft: They do not apply to the rental of luxurious apartments or single-family houses with six or more living rooms (excluding the kitchen).
OR Art. 253b Abs. 2.change_note: 'They' replaced by what it refers to, so the summary stands alone.

OR Art. 253b Abs. 3.summary: The provisions on contesting abusive rents do not apply to residential spaces whose provision has been subsidized by the public sector and whose rents are controlled by an authority.
OR Art. 253b Abs. 3.draft: The provisions on contesting abusive rents do not apply to residential spaces whose provision has been subsidized by the public sector and whose rents are controlled by an authority.

OR Art. 254.summary: A tied transaction linked to the rental of residential or business premises is void if concluding or continuing the lease is made conditional on it and the tenant thereby takes on an obligation to the landlord or a third party that is not directly connected with the use of the rented property.
OR Art. 254.draft: A lease agreement is void if its conclusion or continuation is made dependent on a separate transaction, and the tenant thereby assumes an obligation to the landlord or a third party that is not directly related to the use of the leased property.
OR Art. 254.change_note: Draft said the lease is void; the text makes the tied transaction void, not the lease.

OR Art. 255 Abs. 1.summary: The rental agreement may be for a fixed term or an indefinite term.
OR Art. 255 Abs. 1.draft: The rental agreement may be for a fixed term or an indefinite term.

OR Art. 255 Abs. 2.summary: A lease is fixed-term if it is meant to end, without notice of termination, when the agreed period expires.
OR Art. 255 Abs. 2.draft: The lease ends automatically at the end of the agreed term without the need for a notice of termination. This applies only when the lease was agreed to be for a fixed duration.
OR Art. 255 Abs. 2.change_note: Rephrased as the definition it is; removed an added sentence.

OR Art. 255 Abs. 3.summary: All other leases are of indefinite duration.
OR Art. 255 Abs. 3.draft: The remaining rental agreements are considered indefinite. This applies unless the rental agreement is terminated by either party with a notice period of at least three months.
OR Art. 255 Abs. 3.change_note: Removed an invented condition about a three-month notice period.

OR Art. 256 Abs. 1.summary: The landlord must hand over the property at the agreed time in a condition fit for the intended use, and keep it in that condition.
OR Art. 256 Abs. 1.draft: The landlord must deliver the property at the agreed time in a condition suitable for the intended use and maintain it in that condition. This obligation applies unless otherwise agreed or required by law.
OR Art. 256 Abs. 1.change_note: Removed an invented exception ('unless otherwise agreed or required by law'); Abs. 2 limits deviating agreements.

OR Art. 256 Abs. 2.summary: Agreements that depart from this duty to the tenant's disadvantage are void if they are contained in: a. pre-formulated general terms and conditions; b. leases of residential or business premises.
OR Art. 256 Abs. 2.draft: Any agreement that disadvantages the tenant is void if it appears in: a. pre-formulated general terms and conditions; or b. rental contracts for residential or business premises.
OR Art. 256 Abs. 2.change_note: Draft dropped that only agreements deviating from Abs. 1 are meant ('any agreement that disadvantages the tenant' was too wide).

OR Art. 256a Abs. 1.summary: If a return protocol was created when the previous tenancy ended, the landlord must present it to the new tenant for inspection upon handover of the property upon the new tenant's request.
OR Art. 256a Abs. 1.draft: If a return protocol was created when the previous tenancy ended, the landlord must present it to the new tenant for inspection upon handover of the property upon the new tenant's request.

OR Art. 256a Abs. 2.summary: Likewise, the tenant may ask to be told the rent paid under the previous tenancy.
OR Art. 256a Abs. 2.draft: The tenant may request that the amount of the rent from the previous tenancy be disclosed to them. This right applies equally to the tenant.

OR Art. 256b.summary: The landlord bears the charges and public levies connected with the property.
OR Art. 256b.draft: The landlord bears the charges and public levies associated with the property. This obligation does not apply if the lease agreement specifies that the tenant is responsible for these charges.
OR Art. 256b.change_note: Removed an invented exception (lease making the tenant responsible).

OR Art. 257.summary: Rent is the payment the tenant owes the landlord for being given the use of the property.
OR Art. 257.draft: The tenant owes the landlord rent as the consideration for the letting of the property. This obligation applies unless otherwise agreed in writing or by law.
OR Art. 257.change_note: Removed an invented exception ('unless otherwise agreed in writing or by law'); kept as a definition.

OR Art. 257a Abs. 1.summary: Ancillary costs are the payment for services of the landlord or a third party that are connected with the use of the property.
OR Art. 257a Abs. 1.draft: The tenant must pay additional costs, which are the remuneration for services provided by the landlord or a third party that are connected to the use of the property.
OR Art. 257a Abs. 1.change_note: Draft added 'The tenant must pay additional costs', which contradicts Abs. 2 (only if specially agreed); it is a definition.

OR Art. 257a Abs. 2.summary: The tenant must pay ancillary costs only if they have been specifically agreed upon with the landlord.
OR Art. 257a Abs. 2.draft: The tenant must pay ancillary costs only if they have been specifically agreed upon with the landlord.

OR Art. 257b Abs. 1.summary: For residential and commercial spaces, ancillary costs are the landlord's actual expenses for services related to the use of the property, such as heating, hot water, and similar operating costs, as well as public charges resulting from the use of the property.
OR Art. 257b Abs. 1.draft: For residential and commercial spaces, ancillary costs are the landlord's actual expenses for services related to the use of the property, such as heating, hot water, and similar operating costs, as well as public charges resulting from the use of the property.

OR Art. 257b Abs. 2.summary: On request, the landlord must let the tenant inspect the supporting documents (receipts).
OR Art. 257b Abs. 2.draft: The landlord must provide the tenant with access to the documents upon request. This obligation applies only to the documents related to the rental agreement.
OR Art. 257b Abs. 2.change_note: Removed an invented limitation; 'Belege' are the receipts for the ancillary costs.

OR Art. 257c.summary: The tenant must pay the rent and any additional costs by the end of each month, or at the latest by the end of the rental period, unless another time is agreed upon or is customary in the area.
OR Art. 257c.draft: The tenant must pay the rent and any additional costs by the end of each month, or at the latest by the end of the rental period, unless another time is agreed upon or is customary in the area.

OR Art. 257d Abs. 1.summary: If the tenant falls behind in paying due rent or ancillary costs after taking possession of the property, the landlord may set a written payment deadline and threaten to terminate the lease if the deadline passes unused. This deadline must be at least ten days, and at least 30 days for residential or business premises.
OR Art. 257d Abs. 1.draft: If the tenant falls behind in paying due rent or ancillary costs after taking possession of the property, the landlord may set a written payment deadline and threaten to terminate the lease if the deadline passes unused. This deadline must be at least ten days, and at least 30 days for residential or business premises.

OR Art. 257d Abs. 2.summary: If the tenant does not pay within the deadline, the landlord may terminate the lease without notice; for residential and business premises, with at least 30 days' notice to the end of a month.
OR Art. 257d Abs. 2.draft: If the tenant fails to pay within the set timeframe, the landlord may terminate the lease immediately for residential and commercial spaces, but only after providing at least 30 days' notice ending at the end of a month.
OR Art. 257d Abs. 2.change_note: Draft merged the two cases wrongly ('terminate immediately for residential premises, but only after 30 days' notice'): immediate termination applies to other things; residential/business premises need 30 days to month-end.

OR Art. 257e Abs. 1.summary: If a tenant of residential or commercial premises provides a security deposit in money or securities, the landlord must deposit it at a bank in a savings account or a securities account in the tenant's name.
OR Art. 257e Abs. 1.draft: If a tenant of residential or commercial premises provides a security deposit in money or securities, the landlord must deposit it at a bank in a savings account or a securities account in the tenant's name.

OR Art. 257e Abs. 2.summary: For residential premises, the landlord may demand at most three months' rent as security.
OR Art. 257e Abs. 2.draft: The landlord may demand a security deposit of no more than three months' rent for rented residential space. This limit applies when the landlord requires a security deposit for the rental of residential premises.

OR Art. 257e Abs. 3.summary: The bank may only release the security with the consent of both parties, based on a final payment order, or based on a final court judgment. If the landlord has not legally asserted any claim against the tenant within one year after the end of the tenancy, the tenant may demand the bank to return the security.
OR Art. 257e Abs. 3.draft: The bank may only release the security with the consent of both parties, based on a final payment order, or based on a final court judgment. If the landlord has not legally asserted any claim against the tenant within one year after the end of the tenancy, the tenant may demand the bank to return the security.

OR Art. 257e Abs. 4.summary: The cantons may enact supplementary provisions.
OR Art. 257e Abs. 4.draft: The cantons may enact supplementary provisions.

OR Art. 257f Abs. 1.summary: The tenant must use the property with care.
OR Art. 257f Abs. 1.draft: The tenant must use the property with care. This obligation applies unless the lease agreement or law permits a different use.

OR Art. 257f Abs. 2.summary: The tenant of immovable property must show consideration for other residents of the building and for neighbours.
OR Art. 257f Abs. 2.draft: The tenant of an immovable property must show consideration to the other occupants of the house and to the neighbours. This obligation applies unless the landlord has expressly permitted otherwise.

OR Art. 257f Abs. 3.summary: If, despite a written warning from the landlord, the tenant keeps breaching the duty of care or consideration so that the landlord or the other residents can no longer reasonably be expected to continue the lease, the landlord may terminate without notice; for residential and business premises, with at least 30 days' notice to the end of a month.
OR Art. 257f Abs. 3.draft: If, after a written warning from the landlord, the tenant continues to breach their duty of care or consideration to the extent that the landlord or other residents can no longer reasonably tolerate the continuation of the tenancy, the landlord may terminate the lease immediately for residential or commercial premises, provided a notice period of at least 30 days to the end of a month is given.
OR Art. 257f Abs. 3.change_note: Same error as 257d Abs. 2: draft merged immediate termination and the 30-day rule for residential/business premises.

OR Art. 257f Abs. 4.summary: The landlord of residential or commercial premises may terminate the lease immediately if the tenant intentionally causes severe damage to the property.
OR Art. 257f Abs. 4.draft: The landlord of residential or commercial premises may terminate the lease immediately if the tenant intentionally causes severe damage to the property.

OR Art. 257g Abs. 1.summary: The tenant must report to the landlord defects that the tenant does not have to remedy themselves.
OR Art. 257g Abs. 1.draft: The tenant must notify the landlord of any defects that the tenant is not required to fix themselves. This obligation applies to all defects the tenant is not responsible for remedying.

OR Art. 257g Abs. 2.summary: If the tenant fails to report such a defect, the tenant is liable for the resulting damage to the landlord.
OR Art. 257g Abs. 2.draft: If the tenant fails to report something, the tenant is liable for any damage this omission causes to the landlord.
OR Art. 257g Abs. 2.change_note: 'Something' replaced by 'such a defect' (the duty concerns defects under Abs. 1).

OR Art. 257h Abs. 1.summary: The tenant must tolerate work on the property if it is necessary to eliminate defects, remedy or prevent damage.
OR Art. 257h Abs. 1.draft: The tenant must tolerate work on the property if it is necessary to eliminate defects, remedy or prevent damage.

OR Art. 257h Abs. 2.summary: The tenant must permit the landlord to inspect the property if this is necessary for maintenance, sale, or re-rental.
OR Art. 257h Abs. 2.draft: The tenant must permit the landlord to inspect the property if this is necessary for maintenance, sale, or re-rental.

OR Art. 257h Abs. 3.summary: The landlord must notify the tenant of any work or inspections in a timely manner and consider the tenant's interests during their execution; any claims the tenant may have for rent reduction (Art. 259d) or compensation for damages (Art. 259e) are reserved.
OR Art. 257h Abs. 3.draft: The landlord must notify the tenant of any work or inspections in a timely manner and consider the tenant's interests during their execution; any claims the tenant may have for rent reduction (Art. 259d) or compensation for damages (Art. 259e) are reserved.

OR Art. 258 Abs. 1.summary: If the landlord does not hand over the property at the agreed time or with defects that exclude or significantly impair its suitability for the intended use, the tenant may take action under Articles 107–109 regarding non-performance of contracts.
OR Art. 258 Abs. 1.draft: If the landlord does not hand over the property at the agreed time or with defects that exclude or significantly impair its suitability for the intended use, the tenant may take action under Articles 107–109 regarding non-performance of contracts.

OR Art. 258 Abs. 2.summary: If the tenant accepts the property despite these defects and insists on proper contract performance, they may only assert the claims that would be due to them if defects arose during the rental period (Art. 259a–259i).
OR Art. 258 Abs. 2.draft: If the tenant accepts the property despite these defects and insists on proper contract performance, they may only assert the claims that would be due to them if defects arose during the rental period (Art. 259a–259i).

OR Art. 258 Abs. 3.summary: The tenant may assert claims under Articles 259a–259i if the property has defects at handover that either (a) reduce its suitability for the agreed use without excluding or significantly impairing it, or (b) the tenant would have to remedy at their own expense during the lease term (Article 259).
OR Art. 258 Abs. 3.draft: The tenant may assert claims under Articles 259a–259i if the property has defects at handover that either (a) reduce its suitability for the agreed use without excluding or significantly impairing it, or (b) the tenant would have to remedy at their own expense during the lease term (Article 259).

OR Art. 259.summary: The tenant must remedy defects that can be fixed by small cleaning or repairs necessary for ordinary upkeep, at their own expense, according to local custom.
OR Art. 259.draft: The tenant must remedy defects that can be fixed by small cleaning or repairs necessary for ordinary upkeep, at their own expense, according to local custom.

OR Art. 259a Abs. 1.summary: If defects arise in the leased property that the tenant is neither responsible for nor must remedy at their own expense, or if the tenant is disturbed in the contractual use of the property, the tenant may demand that the landlord: a. remedy the defect; b. reduce the rent proportionally; c. provide compensation; d. assume the legal dispute with a third party.
OR Art. 259a Abs. 1.draft: If defects arise in the leased property that the tenant is neither responsible for nor must remedy at their own expense, or if the tenant is disturbed in the contractual use of the property, the tenant may demand that the landlord: a. remedy the defect; b. reduce the rent proportionally; c. provide compensation; d. assume the legal dispute with a third party.

OR Art. 259a Abs. 2.summary: A tenant of immovable property may also deposit the rent.
OR Art. 259a Abs. 2.draft: A tenant of an immovable property may also deposit the rent. This applies only if the landlord is a natural person or a legal entity whose business consists exclusively or predominantly of letting immovable property.
OR Art. 259a Abs. 2.change_note: Removed an invented condition about the landlord being a natural person or a property company.

OR Art. 259c.summary: The tenant has no claim to have the defect removed if the landlord provides full-value replacement for the defective item within a reasonable time.
OR Art. 259c.draft: The tenant has no claim to have the defect removed if the landlord provides full-value replacement for the defective item within a reasonable time.

OR Art. 259d.summary: If the fitness of the property for its intended use is impaired or reduced, the tenant may demand that the landlord reduce the rent accordingly, from the time the landlord learned of the defect until it is remedied.
OR Art. 259d.draft: If a defect impairs or reduces the suitability of the rented property for its intended use, the tenant may demand that the landlord reduce the rent from the time the tenant became aware of the defect until the defect is remedied.
OR Art. 259d.change_note: Wrong party: the reduction runs from when the LANDLORD learned of the defect ('er' = Vermieter), not the tenant; 'accordingly' (proportionate) restored.

OR Art. 259e.summary: If the tenant has suffered damage due to a defect, the landlord must compensate the tenant, unless the landlord proves that no fault is attributable to them.
OR Art. 259e.draft: If the tenant has suffered damage due to a defect, the landlord must compensate the tenant, unless the landlord proves that no fault is attributable to them.

OR Art. 259f.summary: If a third party asserts a claim to the property that conflicts with the tenant's rights, the landlord must take over the legal dispute upon the tenant's notice.
OR Art. 259f.draft: If a third party asserts a claim to the property that conflicts with the tenant's rights, the landlord must take over the legal dispute upon the tenant's notice.

OR Art. 259g Abs. 1.summary: If a tenant of an immovable property requests the landlord to remedy a defect, the tenant must set a reasonable written deadline for this and may threaten to deposit future due rents with a cantonal designated authority if the deadline passes unused. The tenant must notify the landlord of this deposit in writing.
OR Art. 259g Abs. 1.draft: If a tenant of an immovable property requests the landlord to remedy a defect, the tenant must set a reasonable written deadline for this and may threaten to deposit future due rents with a cantonal designated authority if the deadline passes unused. The tenant must notify the landlord of this deposit in writing.

OR Art. 259g Abs. 2.summary: Once deposited, the rent counts as paid.
OR Art. 259g Abs. 2.draft: With the deposit, the rent is considered paid. This applies only if the landlord has not yet received the rent.
OR Art. 259g Abs. 2.change_note: Removed an invented condition ('only if the landlord has not yet received the rent').

OR Art. 259h Abs. 1.summary: Deposited rents belong to the landlord if the tenant has not asserted their claims against the landlord to the conciliation authority within 30 days of the due date of the first deposited rent.
OR Art. 259h Abs. 1.draft: Deposited rents belong to the landlord if the tenant has not asserted their claims against the landlord to the conciliation authority within 30 days of the due date of the first deposited rent.

OR Art. 259h Abs. 2.summary: As soon as the tenant has announced the deposit, the landlord may ask the conciliation authority to release to the landlord any rent that was wrongly deposited.
OR Art. 259h Abs. 2.draft: The landlord may request the return of wrongfully deposited rent from the conciliation authority once the tenant has notified the landlord of the deposit.
OR Art. 259h Abs. 2.change_note: 'Return' was ambiguous about who receives the money; Herausgabe is release to the landlord.

OR Art. 259i.summary: The procedure is governed by the Civil Procedure Code (ZPO).
OR Art. 259i.draft: The procedure is governed by the Swiss Code of Civil Procedure (ZPO). There are no exceptions to this rule.
OR Art. 259i.change_note: Removed an added sentence ('There are no exceptions').

OR Art. 260 Abs. 1.summary: The landlord may only carry out renovations or alterations to the property if they are reasonable for the tenant and if the tenancy has not been terminated.
OR Art. 260 Abs. 1.draft: The landlord may only carry out renovations or alterations to the property if they are reasonable for the tenant and if the tenancy has not been terminated.

OR Art. 260 Abs. 2.summary: The landlord must consider the tenant's interests when carrying out the work; any claims the tenant may have for rent reduction under Article 259d and for damages under Article 259e are reserved.
OR Art. 260 Abs. 2.draft: The landlord must consider the tenant's interests when carrying out the work; any claims the tenant may have for rent reduction under Article 259d and for damages under Article 259e are reserved.

OR Art. 260a Abs. 1.summary: The tenant may renovate or alter the property only with the landlord's written consent.
OR Art. 260a Abs. 1.draft: The tenant may only carry out renewals and changes to the property if the landlord has given written consent. This requirement applies to all such actions by the tenant.

OR Art. 260a Abs. 2.summary: If the landlord has consented, they may only demand the restoration of the previous condition if this was agreed in writing.
OR Art. 260a Abs. 2.draft: If the landlord has consented, they may only demand the restoration of the previous condition if this was agreed in writing.

OR Art. 260a Abs. 3.summary: When a tenancy ends, if the property has gained significant additional value due to renovations or changes the landlord approved, the tenant may demand a corresponding compensation; any further compensation claims agreed upon in writing are reserved.
OR Art. 260a Abs. 3.draft: When a tenancy ends, if the property has gained significant additional value due to renovations or changes the landlord approved, the tenant may demand a corresponding compensation; any further compensation claims agreed upon in writing are reserved.

OR Art. 261 Abs. 1.summary: If the landlord transfers ownership of the property after the lease was concluded, or loses it in debt enforcement or bankruptcy proceedings, the lease passes to the new owner together with ownership.
OR Art. 261 Abs. 1.draft: If the landlord sells the rental property after the lease is signed or if it is taken from the landlord in a debt enforcement or bankruptcy proceeding, the lease transfers to the new owner of the property.
OR Art. 261 Abs. 1.change_note: 'Sells'/'signed' replaced: Veräusserung covers any transfer of ownership, and the lease is 'concluded'.

OR Art. 261 Abs. 2.summary: The new owner may, however: a. for residential and business premises, terminate the lease with the statutory notice period for the next statutory date if they claim an urgent need for themselves, close relatives or relatives by marriage; b. for other things, terminate the lease with the statutory notice period for the next statutory date if the contract does not allow earlier termination.
OR Art. 261 Abs. 2.draft: The new owner may terminate the lease of residential or commercial premises with the statutory notice period on the next statutory date if they assert an urgent need for themselves, close relatives, or in-laws; for any other item, the new owner may terminate the lease with the statutory notice period on the next statutory date if the contract does not permit earlier termination.

OR Art. 261 Abs. 3.summary: If the new owner terminates the lease earlier than the contract with the previous landlord would have permitted, the previous landlord is liable to the tenant for all resulting damage.
OR Art. 261 Abs. 3.draft: If the new owner terminates the lease earlier than the contract with the previous landlord would have permitted, the previous landlord is liable to the tenant for all resulting damage.

OR Art. 261 Abs. 4.summary: Any provisions regarding expropriation remain unaffected.
OR Art. 261 Abs. 4.draft: Any provisions regarding expropriation remain unaffected.

OR Art. 261a.summary: The rules on transfer of the property apply by analogy when the landlord grants a third party a limited right in rem and this amounts to a change of ownership.
OR Art. 261a.draft: The provisions on the sale of the property apply by analogy when the landlord grants a third party a limited real right, and this is equivalent to a change of ownership. This applies only when the landlord grants a third party a limited real right that is equivalent to a change of ownership.

OR Art. 261b Abs. 1.summary: For the lease of real property (Grundstück), the parties may agree to have the lease noted (vorgemerkt) in the land register.
OR Art. 261b Abs. 1.draft: When renting a plot of land, it is possible to agree that the relationship is noted in the land register.
OR Art. 261b Abs. 1.change_note: 'Plot of land' was too narrow: Grundstück in Swiss law includes buildings and condominium units.

OR Art. 261b Abs. 2.summary: The annotation means that every new owner must let the tenant use the property as the lease provides.
OR Art. 261b Abs. 2.draft: The notice requires every new owner of the property to permit the tenant to use the property in accordance with the lease agreement.
OR Art. 261b Abs. 2.change_note: 'Notice' replaced by 'annotation' to avoid confusion with a notice of termination.

OR Art. 262 Abs. 1.summary: The tenant may sublet the property entirely or partially only with the landlord's consent.
OR Art. 262 Abs. 1.draft: The tenant may sublet the property entirely or partially only with the landlord's consent.

OR Art. 262 Abs. 2.summary: The landlord may only refuse consent if: (a) the tenant refuses to disclose the subletting conditions to the landlord; (b) the subletting conditions are abusive compared to those of the main lease; or (c) the subletting causes substantial disadvantages to the landlord.
OR Art. 262 Abs. 2.draft: The landlord may only refuse consent if: (a) the tenant refuses to disclose the subletting conditions to the landlord; (b) the subletting conditions are abusive compared to those of the main lease; or (c) the subletting causes substantial disadvantages to the landlord.

OR Art. 262 Abs. 3.summary: The tenant is liable to the landlord for ensuring that the subtenant uses the property only as the tenant is permitted to. The landlord may require this of the subtenant directly.
OR Art. 262 Abs. 3.draft: The subtenant must use the property only as permitted to the tenant. The landlord may directly instruct the subtenant to do so.
OR Art. 262 Abs. 3.change_note: Draft dropped the tenant's liability to the landlord, the core of the rule.

OR Art. 263 Abs. 1.summary: A tenant of business premises may transfer the lease to a third party only with the written consent of the landlord.
OR Art. 263 Abs. 1.draft: A tenant of business premises may transfer the lease to a third party only with the written consent of the landlord.

OR Art. 263 Abs. 2.summary: The landlord may refuse consent to the transfer only for good cause (wichtiger Grund).
OR Art. 263 Abs. 2.draft: The landlord may only refuse consent for a sublease for a valid reason.
OR Art. 263 Abs. 2.change_note: Draft said 'sublease'; this article is about transfer of a business lease, not subletting.

OR Art. 263 Abs. 3.summary: If the landlord agrees, the third party replaces the tenant in the rental agreement.
OR Art. 263 Abs. 3.draft: If the landlord agrees, the third party replaces the tenant in the rental agreement.

OR Art. 263 Abs. 4.summary: The original tenant is released from their obligations to the landlord, but remains jointly and severally liable with the third party until the lease ends, or could be ended, under the contract or the law, and for at most two years.
OR Art. 263 Abs. 4.draft: The tenant is released from their obligations to the landlord but remains jointly liable with the third party for up to two years, or until the lease ends according to the contract or law, whichever occurs first.
OR Art. 263 Abs. 4.change_note: Draft dropped 'or could be ended' and restated the cap loosely.

OR Art. 264 Abs. 1.summary: If the tenant returns the property without observing the notice period or termination date, they are only released from their obligations to the landlord if they propose a new tenant who is reasonable for the landlord, is solvent, and is willing to assume the lease on the same terms.
OR Art. 264 Abs. 1.draft: If the tenant returns the property without observing the notice period or termination date, they are only released from their obligations to the landlord if they propose a new tenant who is reasonable for the landlord, is solvent, and is willing to assume the lease on the same terms.

OR Art. 264 Abs. 2.summary: If the tenant does not do so, they must pay the rent until the rental relationship ends or can be ended according to the contract or law.
OR Art. 264 Abs. 2.draft: If the tenant does not do so, they must pay the rent until the rental relationship ends or can be ended according to the contract or law.

OR Art. 264 Abs. 3.summary: The landlord must account for: a. any expenses they save, and b. any gain they obtain or intentionally fail to obtain through alternative use of the property.
OR Art. 264 Abs. 3.draft: The landlord must account for: a. any expenses they save, and b. any gain they obtain or intentionally fail to obtain through alternative use of the property.

OR Art. 265.summary: The landlord and the tenant cannot waive in advance the right to set off claims and debts arising from the lease against each other.
OR Art. 265.draft: The landlord and the tenant may not waive in advance the right to offset claims and debts arising from the tenancy. This prohibition applies to all such claims and debts between the landlord and the tenant.

OR Art. 266 Abs. 1.summary: If the parties have agreed on a specific duration, either explicitly or implicitly, the tenancy ends automatically upon the expiration of that duration without the need for a notice of termination.
OR Art. 266 Abs. 1.draft: If the parties have agreed on a specific duration, either explicitly or implicitly, the tenancy ends automatically upon the expiration of that duration without the need for a notice of termination.

OR Art. 266 Abs. 2.summary: If the parties tacitly continue the lease, it is treated as a lease of indefinite duration.
OR Art. 266 Abs. 2.draft: If the parties continue the tenancy without express agreement, it is deemed an unlimited-term tenancy.

OR Art. 266a Abs. 1.summary: The parties may terminate the open-ended tenancy by observing the statutory notice periods and dates, provided they have not agreed to a longer notice period or a different termination date.
OR Art. 266a Abs. 1.draft: The parties may terminate the open-ended tenancy by observing the statutory notice periods and dates, provided they have not agreed to a longer notice period or a different termination date.

OR Art. 266a Abs. 2.summary: If a party does not observe the notice period or the termination date, the notice takes effect for the next possible termination date.
OR Art. 266a Abs. 2.draft: If the parties fail to meet the deadline or appointment, the termination is effective for the next possible date.
OR Art. 266a Abs. 2.change_note: 'Appointment' was a mistranslation of Termin (termination date).

OR Art. 266b.summary: When renting immovable property or movable structures, the parties may terminate the lease with a three-month notice period on a customary local date, or if no such custom exists, at the end of a six-month rental period.
OR Art. 266b.draft: When renting immovable property or movable structures, the parties may terminate the lease with a three-month notice period on a customary local date, or if no such custom exists, at the end of a six-month rental period.

OR Art. 266c.summary: When renting an apartment, the parties may terminate the lease with a three-month notice period on a customary local date, or if no such custom exists, at the end of a three-month rental period.
OR Art. 266c.draft: When renting an apartment, the parties may terminate the lease with a three-month notice period on a customary local date, or if no such custom exists, at the end of a three-month rental period.

OR Art. 266d.summary: When renting business premises, the parties may terminate the lease with a six-month notice period on a customary local date, or if no such custom exists, at the end of a three-month rental period.
OR Art. 266d.draft: When renting business premises, the parties may terminate the lease with a six-month notice period on a customary local date, or if no such custom exists, at the end of a three-month rental period.

OR Art. 266e.summary: For furnished rooms and separately rented parking spaces or similar facilities, the parties may terminate with two weeks' notice to the end of a one-month rental period.
OR Art. 266e.draft: Parties may terminate the lease of furnished rooms, separately rented parking spaces, or similar facilities with a two-week notice at the end of a one-month rental period. This applies only to furnished rooms, separately rented parking spaces, or similar facilities.

OR Art. 266f.summary: When renting movable property, the parties may terminate the rental agreement with a three-day notice for any date they choose.
OR Art. 266f.draft: When renting movable property, the parties may terminate the rental agreement with a three-day notice for any date they choose.

OR Art. 266g Abs. 1.summary: For important reasons that make continuing the contract unreasonable for them, the parties may terminate the lease with the statutory notice period, to take effect on any date.
OR Art. 266g Abs. 1.draft: Parties may terminate the lease at any time with the statutory notice period if important reasons make fulfilling the contract unreasonable for them.
OR Art. 266g Abs. 1.change_note: 'At any time' clarified: the notice may take effect on any date, but the statutory notice period still applies.

OR Art. 266g Abs. 2.summary: The court decides the financial consequences of the early termination, taking all circumstances into account.
OR Art. 266g Abs. 2.draft: The judge determines the financial consequences of early termination by considering all circumstances. This applies when the termination is not due to the fault of the spouse or registered partner.
OR Art. 266g Abs. 2.change_note: Removed an invented condition about fault of a spouse or registered partner.

OR Art. 266h Abs. 1.summary: If the tenant goes bankrupt after taking possession of the property, the landlord may demand security for future rent payments. The landlord must give the tenant and the bankruptcy administration a written notice of a reasonable period to provide this security.
OR Art. 266h Abs. 1.draft: If the tenant goes bankrupt after taking possession of the property, the landlord may demand security for future rent payments. The landlord must give the tenant and the bankruptcy administration a written notice of a reasonable period to provide this security.

OR Art. 266h Abs. 2.summary: If the landlord does not receive the security within this time limit, they may terminate the lease without notice.
OR Art. 266h Abs. 2.draft: If the landlord does not receive the security within this time limit, they may terminate the lease without notice.

OR Art. 266i.summary: If the tenant dies, their heirs may terminate the lease with the statutory notice period on the next statutory termination date.
OR Art. 266i.draft: If the tenant dies, their heirs may terminate the lease with the statutory notice period on the next statutory termination date.

OR Art. 266k.summary: A tenant of a movable item used for private purposes, which the landlord rents out as part of their business, may terminate the lease with at least 30 days' notice at the end of any three-month rental period. The landlord has no claim to compensation for this termination.
OR Art. 266k.draft: A tenant of a movable item used for private purposes, which the landlord rents out as part of their business, may terminate the lease with at least 30 days' notice at the end of any three-month rental period. The landlord has no claim to compensation for this termination.

OR Art. 266l Abs. 1.summary: Landlords and tenants of residential and business premises must give notice of termination in writing.
OR Art. 266l Abs. 1.draft: Landlords and tenants of residential and commercial spaces must give notice in writing. This requirement applies to both parties.

OR Art. 266l Abs. 2.summary: The landlord must use a cantonal-approved form to give notice, which must specify how the tenant can contest the termination or request an extension of the lease.
OR Art. 266l Abs. 2.draft: The landlord must use a cantonal-approved form to give notice, which must specify how the tenant can contest the termination or request an extension of the lease.

OR Art. 266m Abs. 1.summary: If the rented property serves as the family home, one spouse may only terminate the lease with the other spouse's explicit consent.
OR Art. 266m Abs. 1.draft: If the rented property serves as the family home, one spouse may only terminate the lease with the other spouse's explicit consent.

OR Art. 266m Abs. 2.summary: If a spouse cannot obtain this consent, or it is refused without good reason, that spouse may apply to the court.
OR Art. 266m Abs. 2.draft: If a spouse cannot obtain this consent or it is refused without a valid reason, the spouse may appeal to the judge.
OR Art. 266m Abs. 2.change_note: 'Appeal to the judge' suggested an appeal; den Richter anrufen means applying to the court.

OR Art. 266m Abs. 3.summary: The same rule applies by analogy to registered partnerships.
OR Art. 266m Abs. 3.draft: The same rule applies by analogy to registered partnerships.

OR Art. 266n.summary: The landlord's notice of termination and any payment deadline with a threat of termination (Art. 257d) must be served separately on the tenant and on the tenant's spouse or registered partner.
OR Art. 266n.draft: The landlord must serve the notice of termination and any payment deadline notice with a threat of termination (Art. 257d) separately to the tenant and to the tenant's spouse, registered partner, or cohabiting partner.
OR Art. 266n.change_note: Removed 'cohabiting partner': the text covers only spouses and registered partners.

OR Art. 266o.summary: A notice of termination that does not comply with Articles 266l–266n is void.
OR Art. 266o.draft: The termination is invalid if it does not comply with Articles 266l–266n.
OR Art. 266o.change_note: 'Invalid' replaced by 'void' (nichtig), the exact legal consequence.

OR Art. 267 Abs. 1.summary: The tenant must return the property in the condition that results from use in line with the contract.
OR Art. 267 Abs. 1.draft: The tenant must return the property in the condition resulting from its contractual use. This obligation does not apply if the property has deteriorated due to normal wear and tear or if the deterioration was caused by circumstances beyond the tenant's control.
OR Art. 267 Abs. 1.change_note: Removed invented exceptions (wear and tear, circumstances beyond control) that are not in the text.

OR Art. 267 Abs. 2.summary: Agreements in which the tenant precommits to pay compensation upon termination of the lease that includes anything beyond potential damage coverage are void.
OR Art. 267 Abs. 2.draft: Agreements in which the tenant precommits to pay compensation upon termination of the lease that includes anything beyond potential damage coverage are void.

OR Art. 267a Abs. 1.summary: When the property is returned, the landlord must check its condition and immediately notify the tenant of defects the tenant is responsible for.
OR Art. 267a Abs. 1.draft: When returning the property, the landlord must inspect its condition and immediately notify the tenant of any defects for which the tenant is responsible.
OR Art. 267a Abs. 1.change_note: 'When returning the property' wrongly suggested the landlord returns it.

OR Art. 267a Abs. 2.summary: If the landlord fails to do so, they lose their claims, except for defects that were not detectable through a customary inspection.
OR Art. 267a Abs. 2.draft: If the landlord fails to do so, they lose their claims, except for defects that were not detectable through a customary inspection.

OR Art. 267a Abs. 3.summary: If the landlord discovers such (hidden) defects later, the landlord must notify the tenant immediately.
OR Art. 267a Abs. 3.draft: If the landlord later discovers defects, they must immediately report them to the tenant.
OR Art. 267a Abs. 3.change_note: Restored 'such': the rule refers to defects not detectable in a customary inspection (Abs. 2).

OR Art. 268 Abs. 1.summary: The landlord of business premises has a right of retention over movable things in the rented premises that serve to furnish or use them, as security for one year's rent that has fallen due and the current half-year's rent.
OR Art. 268 Abs. 1.draft: The landlord of business premises has a right of retention for a defaulted annual rent and the current half-year rent on movable items located in the rented premises that belong to their furnishing or use. This right applies only to such items.
OR Art. 268 Abs. 1.change_note: 'Defaulted annual rent' clarified (one year's rent already due); removed a redundant added sentence.

OR Art. 268 Abs. 2.summary: The landlord's right of retention covers items brought in by the subtenant only to the extent that the subtenant has not paid their rent.
OR Art. 268 Abs. 2.draft: The landlord's right of retention covers items brought in by the subtenant only to the extent that the subtenant has not paid their rent.

OR Art. 268 Abs. 3.summary: The right of retention does not cover things that the tenant's creditors could not seize.
OR Art. 268 Abs. 3.draft: The creditor of a tenant cannot exercise a retention right on items that the tenant's own creditors could not seize.
OR Art. 268 Abs. 3.change_note: Draft garbled the subject ('the creditor of a tenant cannot exercise'); the limit is on the landlord's retention right.

OR Art. 268a Abs. 1.summary: Third-party rights take priority over the landlord's right of retention for things the landlord knew or should have known did not belong to the tenant, and for stolen, lost or otherwise missing things.
OR Art. 268a Abs. 1.draft: The rights of third parties to items the landlord knew or should have known did not belong to the tenant, as well as to stolen, lost, or otherwise misappropriated items, take precedence over the landlord's right of retention.
OR Art. 268a Abs. 1.change_note: 'Misappropriated' replaced: abhanden gekommen means lost/gone missing, not embezzled.

OR Art. 268a Abs. 2.summary: If the landlord only discovers during the tenancy that items brought in by the tenant do not belong to the tenant, the landlord's right of retention over those items expires unless the landlord terminates the lease agreement at the earliest possible date.
OR Art. 268a Abs. 2.draft: If the landlord only discovers during the tenancy that items brought in by the tenant do not belong to the tenant, the landlord's right of retention over those items expires unless the landlord terminates the lease agreement at the earliest possible date.

OR Art. 268b Abs. 1.summary: If the tenant intends to move out or remove the things in the rented premises, the landlord may, with the help of the competent official office, retain as many items as are needed to cover the landlord's claim.
OR Art. 268b Abs. 1.draft: If the tenant moves out or removes the items located in the rented space, the landlord may, with the assistance of the competent authority, retain as many items as are necessary to cover their claim.
OR Art. 268b Abs. 1.change_note: Restored 'intends to' (will); the right applies before the move, not only after.

OR Art. 268b Abs. 2.summary: Items removed secretly or by force may be brought back into the rented premises with police help within ten days of their removal.
OR Art. 268b Abs. 2.draft: Heimlich or violently removed items may be returned to the rented rooms with police assistance within ten days of their removal.
OR Art. 268b Abs. 2.change_note: Translated the German word 'Heimlich' left in the draft (secretly).

OR Art. 269.summary: Rent is abusive if it yields an excessive return from the rental property or if it is based on an obviously excessive purchase price.
OR Art. 269.draft: Rent is abusive if it yields an excessive return from the rental property or if it is based on an obviously excessive purchase price.

OR Art. 269a.summary: As a rule, rents are not abusive in particular if they: a. are within the range of rents usual in the locality or neighbourhood; b. are justified by cost increases or additional services of the landlord; c. for newer buildings, are within a cost-covering gross return; d. only offset a rent reduction previously granted by restructuring standard market financing costs, and are set out in a payment plan disclosed to the tenant in advance; e. only offset inflation on the risk-bearing capital; f. do not exceed what landlord and tenant associations, or organisations with similar interests, recommend in their framework agreements.
OR Art. 269a.draft: Mietzinse sind in der Regel nicht missbräuchlich, wenn sie insbesondere im Rahmen der orts- oder quartierüblichen Mietzinse liegen, durch Kostensteigerungen oder Mehrleistungen des Vermieters begründet sind, bei neueren Bauten im Rahmen der kostendeckenden Bruttorendite liegen, lediglich dem Ausgleich einer Mietzinsverbilligung dienen, die zuvor durch Umlagerung marktüblicher Finanzierungskosten gewahrt wurde und in einem dem Mieter im Voraus bekanntgegebenen Zahlungsplan festgelegt sind, lediglich die Teuerung auf dem risikotragenden Kapital ausgleichen oder das Ausmass nicht überschreiten, das Vermieter- und Mieterverbände oder Organisationen, die ähnliche Interessen wahrnehmen, in ihren Rahmenverträgen empfehlen.
OR Art. 269a.change_note: Draft was in German (not translated); translated with letters a–f.

OR Art. 269b.summary: The agreement that the rent follows an index is valid only if the rental contract is concluded for at least five years and the national consumer price index is designated as the index.
OR Art. 269b.draft: The agreement that the rent follows an index is valid only if the rental contract is concluded for at least five years and the national consumer price index is designated as the index.

OR Art. 269c.summary: The agreement that the rent increases periodically by a specific amount is valid only if: a. the rental contract is concluded for at least three years; b. the rent is increased at most once per year; and c. the amount of the increase is specified in Swiss francs.
OR Art. 269c.draft: The agreement that the rent increases periodically by a specific amount is valid only if: a. the rental contract is concluded for at least three years; b. the rent is increased at most once per year; and c. the amount of the increase is specified in Swiss francs.

OR Art. 269d Abs. 1.summary: The landlord may increase the rent at any time, with effect from the next possible termination date. The landlord must notify and justify the increase to the tenant on a form approved by the canton at least ten days before the notice period begins.
OR Art. 269d Abs. 1.draft: The landlord may raise the rent at any time to the next possible termination date. The landlord must notify the tenant of the rent increase at least ten days before the start of the notice period on a form approved by the canton, and provide a reason for the increase.
OR Art. 269d Abs. 1.change_note: Clarified 'raise to the next termination date' as 'with effect from'; 'provide a reason' -> notify and justify.

OR Art. 269d Abs. 2.summary: A rent increase is void if the landlord: a. does not communicate it using the prescribed form; b. does not provide a justification; c. threatens or issues a termination notice with the communication.
OR Art. 269d Abs. 2.draft: A rent increase is void if the landlord: a. does not communicate it using the prescribed form; b. does not provide a justification; c. threatens or issues a termination notice with the communication.

OR Art. 269d Abs. 3.summary: The provisions of paragraphs 1 and 2 also apply when the landlord intends to unilaterally alter the lease agreement to the tenant's detriment, specifically by reducing existing services or introducing new ancillary costs.
OR Art. 269d Abs. 3.draft: The provisions of paragraphs 1 and 2 also apply when the landlord intends to unilaterally alter the lease agreement to the tenant's detriment, specifically by reducing existing services or introducing new ancillary costs.

OR Art. 269d Abs. 4.summary: For notice of a rent increase or other unilateral contract change, a mechanically reproduced signature on the prescribed form is sufficient.
OR Art. 269d Abs. 4.draft: For a rent increase or other unilateral contract changes, a mechanically reproduced signature on the prescribed form is sufficient. This applies only to the communication of such changes.

OR Art. 269d Abs. 5.summary: For rent increases stipulated in an agreement under Article 269c, written notice is sufficient.
OR Art. 269d Abs. 5.draft: For rent increases stipulated in an agreement under Article 269c, written notice is sufficient.

OR Art. 270 Abs. 1.summary: Within 30 days of taking over the property, the tenant may challenge the initial rent before the conciliation authority as abusive under Articles 269 and 269a and demand a reduction, if: a. the tenant felt forced to conclude the contract because of personal or family hardship or the situation on the local market for residential and business premises; or b. the landlord significantly increased the initial rent compared with the previous rent for the same property.
OR Art. 270 Abs. 1.draft: The tenant may challenge the initial rent as abusive within 30 days of taking possession and demand its reduction if: (a) they were compelled to sign the contract due to personal or family hardship or local housing market conditions; or (b) the landlord significantly increased the initial rent compared to the previous rent for the same property.
OR Art. 270 Abs. 1.change_note: Restored the conciliation authority as forum and the reference to Art. 269/269a; 'sign' -> 'conclude'.

OR Art. 270 Abs. 2.summary: In cases of housing shortage, the cantons may make the use of the form according to Article 269d obligatory for their territory or a part thereof when concluding a new lease agreement.
OR Art. 270 Abs. 2.draft: In cases of housing shortage, the cantons may make the use of the form according to Article 269d obligatory for their territory or a part thereof when concluding a new lease agreement.

OR Art. 270a Abs. 1.summary: The tenant may challenge the rent as abusive and demand a reduction to the next possible termination date if they have reason to believe the landlord is earning an excessive return on the rental property due to a substantial change in the calculation basis, particularly a cost reduction, in violation of Articles 269 and 269a.
OR Art. 270a Abs. 1.draft: The tenant may challenge the rent as abusive and demand a reduction to the next possible termination date if they have reason to believe the landlord is earning an excessive return on the rental property due to a substantial change in the calculation basis, particularly a cost reduction, in violation of Articles 269 and 269a.

OR Art. 270a Abs. 2.summary: The tenant must submit a written request for rent reduction to the landlord, who must respond within 30 days. If the landlord does not grant the request, only grants it partially, or fails to respond within the 30-day period, the tenant may refer the matter to the conciliation authority within 30 days.
OR Art. 270a Abs. 2.draft: The tenant must submit a written request for rent reduction to the landlord, who must respond within 30 days. If the landlord does not grant the request, only grants it partially, or fails to respond within the 30-day period, the tenant may refer the matter to the conciliation authority within 30 days.

OR Art. 270a Abs. 3.summary: If the tenant files a request for rent reduction at the same time as challenging a rent increase, paragraph 2 does not apply.
OR Art. 270a Abs. 3.draft: If the tenant files a request for rent reduction at the same time as challenging a rent increase, paragraph 2 does not apply.

OR Art. 270b Abs. 1.summary: The tenant may challenge a rent increase as abusive under Articles 269 and 269a at the conciliation authority within 30 days of receiving notice of the increase.
OR Art. 270b Abs. 1.draft: The tenant may challenge a rent increase as abusive under Articles 269 and 269a at the conciliation authority within 30 days of receiving notice of the increase.

OR Art. 270b Abs. 2.summary: If the landlord unilaterally changes the rental contract to the tenant's disadvantage—such as reducing previous services or introducing new ancillary costs—paragraph 1 applies.
OR Art. 270b Abs. 2.draft: If the landlord unilaterally changes the rental contract to the tenant's disadvantage—such as reducing previous services or introducing new ancillary costs—paragraph 1 applies.

OR Art. 270c.summary: Apart from challenging the initial rent, a party can only argue before the conciliation authority that the rent increase or reduction demanded by the other party is not justified by a corresponding change in the index.
OR Art. 270c.draft: A party may only claim before the conciliation authority that the rent increase or decrease demanded by the other party is not justified by a corresponding change in the index, provided that the initial rent is not being contested.
OR Art. 270c.change_note: Draft reversed the reservation ('provided the initial rent is not being contested'); 'unter Vorbehalt' means the initial-rent challenge remains available.

OR Art. 270d.summary: Apart from challenging the initial rent, the tenant cannot contest stepped (graduated) rents.
OR Art. 270d.draft: The tenant cannot contest graduated rent increases, provided that the initial rent is subject to challenge.
OR Art. 270d.change_note: Draft reversed the reservation ('provided that the initial rent is subject to challenge').

OR Art. 270e.summary: The existing rental agreement continues unchanged: a. during the conciliation procedure if no agreement is reached between the parties, and b. during the court proceedings, subject to any provisional measures ordered by the judge.
OR Art. 270e.draft: The existing rental agreement continues unchanged: a. during the conciliation procedure if no agreement is reached between the parties, and b. during the court proceedings, subject to any provisional measures ordered by the judge.

OR Art. 271 Abs. 1.summary: A notice of termination can be challenged if it breaches the principle of good faith.
OR Art. 271 Abs. 1.draft: A tenancy termination is contestable if it violates the principle of good faith.
OR Art. 271 Abs. 1.change_note: Wording ('notice of termination' as the act being challenged).

OR Art. 271 Abs. 2.summary: On request, the reasons for the termination must be given.
OR Art. 271 Abs. 2.draft: The landlord must provide a written explanation of the termination upon request. This obligation applies to all terminations covered by this provision.
OR Art. 271 Abs. 2.change_note: Draft limited it to the landlord and added 'written'; the text applies to either party and sets no written form.

OR Art. 271a Abs. 1.summary: A landlord's notice of termination can be challenged in particular if it is given: a. because the tenant asserts claims under the lease in good faith; b. because the landlord wants to impose a unilateral change to the tenant's detriment or a rent adjustment; c. solely to make the tenant buy the rented flat; d. during conciliation or court proceedings connected with the lease, unless the tenant started them abusively; e. within three years after the end of conciliation or court proceedings connected with the lease in which the landlord: 1. lost to a significant extent; 2. withdrew or substantially reduced the claim or action; 3. decided not to go to court; 4. reached a settlement or other agreement with the tenant; f. because of changes in the tenant's family situation that cause the landlord no significant disadvantage.
OR Art. 271a Abs. 1.draft: The landlord's termination is contestable if it is given because the tenant asserts rights under the lease in good faith; because the landlord seeks to impose a unilateral contract change or rent adjustment to the tenant's detriment; solely to induce the tenant to purchase the rented apartment; during a conciliation or court proceeding related to the lease, unless the tenant initiated the proceeding abusively; within three years after the conclusion of such a related proceeding in which the landlord: 1. was substantially defeated; 2. withdrew or significantly reduced their claim or lawsuit; 3. waived to call upon the judge; 4. reached a settlement or otherwise agreed with the tenant; or because of changes in the tenant's family situation that do not cause the landlord any substantial disadvantage.
OR Art. 271a Abs. 1.change_note: Restored 'in particular' (the list is not exhaustive) and letters a–f; fixed 'waived to call upon the judge'.

OR Art. 271a Abs. 2.summary: Paragraph 1, letter e also applies if the tenant can prove with written documents that they have reached an agreement with the landlord on a claim arising from the tenancy outside of a conciliation or court proceeding.
OR Art. 271a Abs. 2.draft: Paragraph 1, letter e also applies if the tenant can prove with written documents that they have reached an agreement with the landlord on a claim arising from the tenancy outside of a conciliation or court proceeding.

OR Art. 271a Abs. 3.summary: Paragraph 1, letters d and e do not apply to terminations of tenancy for: (a) urgent personal need of the landlord for themselves, close relatives, or in-laws; (b) tenant's arrears in payment (Art. 257d); (c) serious breach by the tenant of their duty to exercise diligence and consideration (Art. 257f para. 3 and 4); (d) sale of the property (Art. 261); (e) important reasons (Art. 266g); (f) tenant's bankruptcy (Art. 266h).
OR Art. 271a Abs. 3.draft: Paragraph 1, letters d and e do not apply to terminations of tenancy for: (a) urgent personal need of the landlord for themselves, close relatives, or in-laws; (b) tenant's arrears in payment (Art. 257d); (c) serious breach by the tenant of their duty to exercise diligence and consideration (Art. 257f para. 3 and 4); (d) sale of the property (Art. 261); (e) important reasons (Art. 266g); (f) tenant's bankruptcy (Art. 266h).

OR Art. 272 Abs. 1.summary: The tenant may request an extension of a fixed-term or open-ended lease if the lease termination would cause a hardship for the tenant or their family that cannot be justified by the landlord's interests.
OR Art. 272 Abs. 1.draft: The tenant may request an extension of a fixed-term or open-ended lease if the lease termination would cause a hardship for the tenant or their family that cannot be justified by the landlord's interests.

OR Art. 272 Abs. 2.summary: When weighing the interests, the competent authority considers in particular: a. the circumstances in which the contract was concluded and its content; b. the duration of the lease; c. the personal, family and financial circumstances of the parties and their conduct; d. any need of the landlord to use the premises for themselves, close relatives or relatives by marriage, and how urgent that need is; e. the situation on the local market for residential and business premises.
OR Art. 272 Abs. 2.draft: The competent authority must consider, in particular: a. the circumstances of the contract's conclusion and its content; b. the duration of the tenancy; c. the personal, family, and economic circumstances of the parties and their conduct; d. any owner's need for the property for themselves, close relatives, or in-laws, along with the urgency of that need; e. the conditions on the local market for residential and commercial spaces.
OR Art. 272 Abs. 2.change_note: 'Any owner's need' corrected to the landlord's own need; restored 'when weighing the interests'.

OR Art. 272 Abs. 3.summary: If a tenant requests a second extension, the competent authority must also consider whether the tenant has taken all reasonable steps to avoid the hardship.
OR Art. 272 Abs. 3.draft: If a tenant requests a second extension, the competent authority must also consider whether the tenant has taken all reasonable steps to avoid the hardship.

OR Art. 272a Abs. 1.summary: The extension of a tenancy is excluded in the case of terminations due to: a) the tenant's arrears in payment (Art. 257d); b) a serious breach by the tenant of their duty to exercise diligence and consideration (Art. 257f para. 3 and 4); c) the tenant's bankruptcy (Art. 266h); or d) a lease contract that was expressly concluded only for the limited period until the start of construction or until the necessary permits are obtained for an upcoming renovation or demolition project.
OR Art. 272a Abs. 1.draft: The extension of a tenancy is excluded in the case of terminations due to: a) the tenant's arrears in payment (Art. 257d); b) a serious breach by the tenant of their duty to exercise diligence and consideration (Art. 257f para. 3 and 4); c) the tenant's bankruptcy (Art. 266h); or d) a lease contract that was expressly concluded only for the limited period until the start of construction or until the necessary permits are obtained for an upcoming renovation or demolition project.

OR Art. 272a Abs. 2.summary: The extension of the lease is generally excluded if the landlord offers the tenant equivalent alternative housing or business premises.
OR Art. 272a Abs. 2.draft: The extension of the lease is generally excluded if the landlord offers the tenant equivalent alternative housing or business premises.

OR Art. 272b Abs. 1.summary: The lease for residential premises may be extended for a maximum of four years, and for business premises for a maximum of six years. Within this maximum duration, one or two extensions may be granted.
OR Art. 272b Abs. 1.draft: The lease for residential premises may be extended for a maximum of four years, and for business premises for a maximum of six years. Within this maximum duration, one or two extensions may be granted.

OR Art. 272b Abs. 2.summary: If the parties agree to extend the lease, there is no maximum duration, and the tenant may waive a second extension.
OR Art. 272b Abs. 2.draft: If the parties agree to extend the lease, there is no maximum duration, and the tenant may waive a second extension.

OR Art. 272c Abs. 1.summary: Either party may ask that the contract be adapted to changed circumstances in the extension decision.
OR Art. 272c Abs. 1.draft: Each party may request that the contract be adjusted to changed circumstances in the extension decision. This applies to every party involved.

OR Art. 272c Abs. 2.summary: If the contract was not changed in the extension decision, it continues unchanged during the extension; the statutory adjustment possibilities are reserved.
OR Art. 272c Abs. 2.draft: If the contract was not changed in the extension decision, it continues unchanged during the extension; the statutory adjustment possibilities are reserved.

OR Art. 272d.summary: If the extension decision or extension agreement does not specify otherwise, the tenant may terminate the lease as follows: a. for an extension of up to one year, with one month's notice on the end of a month; b. for an extension of more than one year, with three months' notice on a legal termination date.
OR Art. 272d.draft: If the extension decision or extension agreement does not specify otherwise, the tenant may terminate the lease as follows: a. for an extension of up to one year, with one month's notice on the end of a month; b. for an extension of more than one year, with three months' notice on a legal termination date.

OR Art. 273 Abs. 1.summary: If one party wishes to contest a termination, they must submit the request to the conciliation authority within 30 days of receiving the termination notice.
OR Art. 273 Abs. 1.draft: If one party wishes to contest a termination, they must submit the request to the conciliation authority within 30 days of receiving the termination notice.

OR Art. 273 Abs. 2.summary: If the tenant seeks an extension of the lease, they must submit the request to the conciliation authority: within 30 days of receiving the notice of termination for an indefinite lease, or at least 60 days before the end of the fixed-term lease.
OR Art. 273 Abs. 2.draft: If the tenant seeks an extension of the lease, they must submit the request to the conciliation authority: within 30 days of receiving the notice of termination for an indefinite lease, or at least 60 days before the end of the fixed-term lease.

OR Art. 273 Abs. 3.summary: The tenant must submit a request for a second extension to the conciliation authority no later than 60 days before the first extension expires.
OR Art. 273 Abs. 3.draft: The tenant must submit a request for a second extension to the conciliation authority no later than 60 days before the first extension expires.

OR Art. 273 Abs. 4.summary: The procedure before the conciliation authority follows the provisions of the Swiss Code of Civil Procedure.
OR Art. 273 Abs. 4.draft: The procedure before the conciliation authority follows the provisions of the Swiss Code of Civil Procedure.

OR Art. 273 Abs. 5.summary: If the competent authority rejects a tenant's request to contest a termination of the lease, it must ex officio examine whether the tenancy can be extended.
OR Art. 273 Abs. 5.draft: If the competent authority rejects a tenant's request to contest a termination of the lease, it must ex officio examine whether the tenancy can be extended.

OR Art. 273a Abs. 1.summary: If the rented property is the family home, the tenant's spouse may also challenge the termination, request an extension of the lease or exercise the other rights the tenant has on termination.
OR Art. 273a Abs. 1.draft: If the rented property serves as the family home, the tenant’s spouse may contest the termination of the lease, request an extension of the rental relationship, or exercise any other rights that belong to the tenant upon termination.
OR Art. 273a Abs. 1.change_note: Restored 'also': the spouse acts in addition to, not instead of, the tenant.

OR Art. 273a Abs. 2.summary: Agreements on extending the lease are valid only if concluded with both spouses.
OR Art. 273a Abs. 2.draft: Agreements to extend visitation rights are only valid if they are concluded with both spouses.
OR Art. 273a Abs. 2.change_note: Serious mistranslation: draft said 'visitation rights'; Erstreckung is the extension of the lease.

OR Art. 273a Abs. 3.summary: The same rule applies by analogy to registered partnerships.
OR Art. 273a Abs. 3.draft: The same rule applies by analogy to registered partnerships.

OR Art. 273b Abs. 1.summary: The section on protection against termination applies to a sublease as long as the main lease has not ended. A sublease can be extended only for as long as the main lease runs.
OR Art. 273b Abs. 1.draft: This section applies to subletting only as long as the main lease remains in effect. The sublet may be extended only for the duration of the main lease.
OR Art. 273b Abs. 1.change_note: 'This section' identified (protection against termination of residential and business leases).

OR Art. 273b Abs. 2.summary: If subletting is primarily intended to circumvent termination protection regulations, the subtenant is granted termination protection regardless of the main lease. If the main lease is terminated, the landlord replaces the tenant in the contract with the subtenant.
OR Art. 273b Abs. 2.draft: If subletting is primarily intended to circumvent termination protection regulations, the subtenant is granted termination protection regardless of the main lease. If the main lease is terminated, the landlord replaces the tenant in the contract with the subtenant.

OR Art. 273c Abs. 1.summary: The tenant can waive rights under the section on protection against termination only where this is expressly provided for.
OR Art. 273c Abs. 1.draft: The tenant may only waive rights granted under this section if such waiver is explicitly provided for.
OR Art. 273c Abs. 1.change_note: 'This section' identified so the summary stands alone.

OR Art. 273c Abs. 2.summary: Agreements to the contrary are void.
OR Art. 273c Abs. 2.draft: No agreements that differ from this provision are valid.
