OR Art. 544 Abs. 1.summary: Things, rights in rem or claims transferred to or acquired for the simple partnership belong to the partners jointly, as set out in the partnership agreement.
OR Art. 544 Abs. 1.draft: Sachen, dingliche Rechte, or Forderungen transferred to or acquired for the company belong jointly to the partners according to the terms of the partnership agreement. This applies only to items transferred to or acquired for the company.
OR Art. 544 Abs. 1.change_note: Draft left German words untranslated, called the simple partnership a 'company', and added a redundant sentence.

OR Art. 544 Abs. 2.summary: Creditors of a partner may only claim their debtor's share of the liquidation proceeds, unless the partnership agreement states otherwise.
OR Art. 544 Abs. 2.draft: Creditors of a partner may only claim their debtor's share of the liquidation proceeds, unless the partnership agreement states otherwise.

OR Art. 544 Abs. 3.summary: If the partners have jointly or through representation entered into obligations with a third party, they are jointly and severally liable to that third party, unless otherwise agreed.
OR Art. 544 Abs. 3.draft: If the partners have jointly or through representation entered into obligations with a third party, they are jointly and severally liable to that third party, unless otherwise agreed.

ZPO Art. 113 Abs. 1.summary: No party compensation (for the other side's costs) is awarded in conciliation proceedings. This does not affect the canton's payment of a legal-aid lawyer appointed free of charge.
ZPO Art. 113 Abs. 1.draft: In the conciliation procedure, no party compensation is awarded. However, the canton may compensate an unpaid legal representative.
ZPO Art. 113 Abs. 1.change_note: 'Unpaid legal representative' mistranslated unentgeltlicher Rechtsbeistand (legal-aid counsel); 'may compensate' replaced by the reservation the text makes.

ZPO Art. 113 Abs. 2.summary: No court fees are charged in disputes: a. under the Equality Act of March 24, 1995; b. under the Disability Equality Act of December 13, 2002; c. concerning the rental and lease of residential and business premises, as well as agricultural lease; d. arising from an employment relationship and under the Employment Services Act of October 6, 1989, up to a dispute value of 30,000 francs; e. under the Participation Act of December 17, 1993; f. concerning supplementary insurance to social health insurance under the Federal Act of March 18, 1994 on Health Insurance; g. under the DSG.
ZPO Art. 113 Abs. 2.draft: No court fees are charged in disputes: a. under the Equality Act of March 24, 1995; b. under the Disability Equality Act of December 13, 2002; c. concerning the rental and lease of residential and business premises, as well as agricultural lease; d. arising from an employment relationship and under the Employment Services Act of October 6, 1989, up to a dispute value of 30,000 francs; e. under the Participation Act of December 17, 1993; f. concerning supplementary insurance to social health insurance under the Federal Act of March 18, 1994 on Health Insurance; g. under the DSG.

ZPO Art. 197.summary: Court proceedings are preceded by an attempt at conciliation before a conciliation authority.
ZPO Art. 197.draft: A court decision must be preceded by an attempt at conciliation before a conciliation authority. This requirement applies to all cases where the value in dispute exceeds CHF 10,000, with exceptions for cases explicitly excluded by law.
ZPO Art. 197.change_note: Removed an invented CHF 10,000 threshold and invented exceptions (exceptions are in Art. 198–199).

ZPO Art. 198.summary: There is no conciliation procedure: a. in summary proceedings; abis. in actions for violence, threats or stalking under Art. 28b ZGB or concerning electronic monitoring under Art. 28c ZGB; b. in actions on civil status; bbis. in actions on maintenance of minor or adult children and other child matters; c. in divorce proceedings; d. in proceedings to dissolve or annul a registered partnership; e. in these debt-enforcement (SchKG) actions: 1. action to deny the debt (Art. 83 para. 2), 2. declaratory action (Art. 85a), 3. third-party ownership action (Art. 106–109), 4. action to join a seizure (Art. 111), 5. actions to separate or add assets to the bankruptcy estate (Art. 242), 6. action contesting the schedule of claims (Art. 148 and 250), 7. action to establish new assets (Art. 265a), 8. action to return retained items (Art. 284); f. in disputes for which a single cantonal instance is competent under Art. 7; g. for principal intervention, counterclaims and third-party actions; h. where the court has set a deadline for an action, and for actions joined to it if they are factually connected; i. in actions before the Federal Patent Court.
ZPO Art. 198.draft: The out-of-court conciliation procedure does not apply in summary proceedings, in lawsuits concerning violence, threats, or stalking under Article 28b ZGB or electronic surveillance under Article 28c ZGB, in lawsuits regarding civil status, in lawsuits concerning maintenance and other child-related matters for minor and adult children, in divorce proceedings, in proceedings to dissolve or declare the invalidity of a registered partnership, in the following claims under the Swiss Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act (SchKG): the denial of debt claim (Art. 83 para. 2 SchKG), the declaratory action (Art. 85a SchKG), the objection action (Art. 106–109 SchKG), the counterclaim (Art. 111 SchKG), the separate or collective action (Art. 242 SchKG), the collocation action (Art. 148 and 250 SchKG), the action to establish new assets (Art. 265a SchKG),
ZPO Art. 198.change_note: Draft was truncated (items e8 and f–i missing), added 'out-of-court', and mistranslated Anschlussklage (as 'counterclaim') and Art. 242 actions.

ZPO Art. 199 Abs. 1.summary: In financial (pecuniary) disputes with a value in dispute of at least CHF 100,000, the parties may jointly waive the conciliation procedure.
ZPO Art. 199 Abs. 1.draft: In disputes concerning property rights with a value of at least 100,000 Swiss francs, the parties may jointly waive the conciliation procedure.

ZPO Art. 199 Abs. 2.summary: The plaintiff may unilaterally waive the conciliation procedure if: a) the defendant has their seat or residence abroad; b) the defendant's place of stay is unknown; or c) the dispute concerns the Equality Act of March 24, 1995.
ZPO Art. 199 Abs. 2.draft: The plaintiff may unilaterally waive the conciliation procedure if: a) the defendant has their seat or residence abroad; b) the defendant's place of stay is unknown; or c) the dispute concerns the Equality Act of March 24, 1995.

ZPO Art. 199 Abs. 3.summary: When disputes fall under the jurisdiction of a single cantonal authority as per Articles 5, 6, and 8, the plaintiff may file the lawsuit directly with the court.
ZPO Art. 199 Abs. 3.draft: When disputes fall under the jurisdiction of a single cantonal authority as per Articles 5, 6, and 8, the plaintiff may file the lawsuit directly with the court.

ZPO Art. 200 Abs. 1.summary: In disputes over the rental or lease of residential and business premises, the conciliation authority consists of a chair and equal (parity) representation of both sides.
ZPO Art. 200 Abs. 1.draft: In disputes concerning the lease or hire of residential and business premises, the conciliation authority consists of one presiding person and one parity representative.
ZPO Art. 200 Abs. 1.change_note: 'One parity representative' was wrong: paritätische Vertretung means equal representation of both sides.

ZPO Art. 200 Abs. 2.summary: In disputes under the Equality Act of March 24, 1995, the conciliation authority consists of a presiding person and a parity representation of the employer and employee sides and the public and private sectors; the genders must be represented equally.
ZPO Art. 200 Abs. 2.draft: In disputes under the Equality Act of March 24, 1995, the conciliation authority consists of a presiding person and a parity representation of the employer and employee sides and the public and private sectors; the genders must be represented equally.

ZPO Art. 201 Abs. 1.summary: The conciliation authority tries to reconcile the parties in an informal hearing. If it helps settle the dispute, a settlement may also include disputed issues between the parties outside the proceedings.
ZPO Art. 201 Abs. 1.draft: The conciliation authority attempts to reconcile the parties in an informal negotiation. If this serves to settle the dispute, issues between the parties that lie outside the proceedings may also be included in a settlement.

ZPO Art. 201 Abs. 2.summary: In matters governed by Article 200, the conciliation authority also serves as a legal advice office.
ZPO Art. 201 Abs. 2.draft: In matters governed by Article 200, the conciliation authority also serves as a legal advice office.

ZPO Art. 202 Abs. 1.summary: The procedure is initiated by a conciliation request, which may be submitted in the forms prescribed by Article 130 or given orally to the conciliation authority for record.
ZPO Art. 202 Abs. 1.draft: The procedure is initiated by a conciliation request, which may be submitted in the forms prescribed by Article 130 or given orally to the conciliation authority for record.

ZPO Art. 202 Abs. 2.summary: In a conciliation request, the opposing party, the legal claim, and the subject of the dispute must be specified.
ZPO Art. 202 Abs. 2.draft: In a conciliation request, the opposing party, the legal claim, and the subject of the dispute must be specified.

ZPO Art. 202 Abs. 3.summary: The conciliation authority serves the request on the other party without delay and at the same time summons the parties to the conciliation hearing.
ZPO Art. 202 Abs. 3.draft: The conciliation authority immediately sends the request for conciliation to the opposing party and simultaneously summons both parties to the mediation.
ZPO Art. 202 Abs. 3.change_note: 'Mediation' replaced (this is the conciliation hearing, not mediation, which the ZPO treats separately).

ZPO Art. 202 Abs. 4.summary: In matters under Article 200, the conciliation authority may exceptionally order an exchange of written submissions if a decision proposal under Article 210 or a decision under Article 212 is possible.
ZPO Art. 202 Abs. 4.draft: In matters governed by Article 200, she may exceptionally conduct a written exchange of statements if a proposal for a decision under Article 210 or a decision under Article 212 is at issue.
ZPO Art. 202 Abs. 4.change_note: 'She' replaced by the conciliation authority; 'at issue' -> possible (in Frage kommt).

ZPO Art. 203 Abs. 1.summary: The hearing must take place within two months of the request being received or after the conclusion of the exchange of written statements.
ZPO Art. 203 Abs. 1.draft: The hearing must take place within two months of the request being received or after the conclusion of the exchange of written statements.

ZPO Art. 203 Abs. 2.summary: The conciliation authority may have any relevant documents presented and may conduct an inspection. If a proposal for a decision under Article 210 or a decision under Article 212 is possible, it may also take the other evidence, provided this does not significantly delay the proceedings.
ZPO Art. 203 Abs. 2.draft: The conciliation authority may have any relevant documents presented and may conduct an inspection. If a proposal for a decision under Article 210 or a decision under Article 212 is possible, it may also take the other evidence, provided this does not significantly delay the proceedings.

ZPO Art. 203 Abs. 3.summary: The hearing is not public. In matters governed by Article 200, the conciliation authority may permit the public wholly or partially if there is a public interest.
ZPO Art. 203 Abs. 3.draft: The hearing is not public. In matters governed by Article 200, the conciliation authority may permit the public wholly or partially if there is a public interest.

ZPO Art. 203 Abs. 4.summary: With the parties' consent, the conciliation authority may hold further hearings. The proceedings must be concluded within twelve months at the latest.
ZPO Art. 203 Abs. 4.draft: With the parties' consent, the conciliation authority may conduct further negotiations. The proceedings must be concluded no later than twelve months later.
ZPO Art. 203 Abs. 4.change_note: 'Negotiations' -> hearings; 'twelve months later' had no reference point.

ZPO Art. 204 Abs. 1.summary: Parties must appear in person at the conciliation hearing. If a legal entity is a party, either an organ or a person must appear who holds a commercial power of attorney, is authorized to conduct the proceedings and conclude a settlement, and is familiar with the subject matter of the dispute.
ZPO Art. 204 Abs. 1.draft: Parties must appear in person at the conciliation hearing. If a legal entity is a party, either an organ or a person must appear who holds a commercial power of attorney, is authorized to conduct the proceedings and conclude a settlement, and is familiar with the subject matter of the dispute.

ZPO Art. 204 Abs. 2.summary: The parties may be accompanied by a legal adviser or a person they trust.
ZPO Art. 204 Abs. 2.draft: Parties may be accompanied by a legal representative, a legal advisor, or a trusted person.
ZPO Art. 204 Abs. 2.change_note: Rechtsbeiständin/Rechtsbeistand are the female and male forms of one term, not two kinds of adviser.

ZPO Art. 204 Abs. 3.summary: A person does not have to appear in person and may be represented if they have an out-of-canton or foreign residence or seat; are prevented due to illness, old age, or other important reasons; in disputes under Article 243, are an employer or insurer who has delegated representation to an employee or a landlord who has delegated it to the property management, provided these representatives are authorized in writing to conclude a settlement; or are one of several plaintiffs or defendants, provided at least one party is present and authorized to represent the other plaintiffs or defendants and conclude a settlement on their behalf.
ZPO Art. 204 Abs. 3.draft: A person does not have to appear in person and may be represented if they have an out-of-canton or foreign residence or seat; are prevented due to illness, old age, or other important reasons; in disputes under Article 243, are an employer or insurer who has delegated representation to an employee or a landlord who has delegated it to the property management, provided these representatives are authorized in writing to conclude a settlement; or are one of several plaintiffs or defendants, provided at least one party is present and authorized to represent the other plaintiffs or defendants and conclude a settlement on their behalf.

ZPO Art. 204 Abs. 4.summary: The other party must be informed in advance about the representation.
ZPO Art. 204 Abs. 4.draft: The opposing party must be informed about the representation in advance. This obligation applies regardless of whether the representation is by a lawyer or another person.

ZPO Art. 205 Abs. 1.summary: Neither the statements of the parties may be recorded in the minutes nor may they be used later in the decision-making process.
ZPO Art. 205 Abs. 1.draft: Neither the statements of the parties may be recorded in the minutes nor may they be used later in the decision-making process.

ZPO Art. 205 Abs. 2.summary: The statements may, however, be used if the conciliation authority makes a decision proposal or a decision.
ZPO Art. 205 Abs. 2.draft: The use of the statements is reserved for the case of a proposal for a decision or a decision by the conciliation authority.
ZPO Art. 205 Abs. 2.change_note: Clarified that the reservation is an exception to Abs. 1 (use is allowed in these cases).

ZPO Art. 206 Abs. 1.summary: If the plaintiff fails to appear, the request for conciliation is deemed withdrawn, and the proceedings are dismissed as having become moot.
ZPO Art. 206 Abs. 1.draft: If the plaintiff fails to appear, the request for conciliation is deemed withdrawn, and the proceedings are dismissed as having become moot.

ZPO Art. 206 Abs. 2.summary: If the defendant party fails to appear, the conciliation authority proceeds as if no agreement had been reached (Articles 209–212).
ZPO Art. 206 Abs. 2.draft: If the defendant party fails to appear, the conciliation authority proceeds as if no agreement had been reached (Articles 209–212).

ZPO Art. 206 Abs. 3.summary: If both parties fail to appear, the proceedings are dismissed as being without object.
ZPO Art. 206 Abs. 3.draft: If both parties fail to appear, the proceedings are dismissed as being without object.

ZPO Art. 206 Abs. 4.summary: A party in default may be given a disciplinary fine of up to CHF 1,000.
ZPO Art. 206 Abs. 4.draft: A party that fails to meet a deadline may be fined up to 1,000 Swiss francs.
ZPO Art. 206 Abs. 4.change_note: 'Fails to meet a deadline' was too narrow/wrong; Säumnis here is default (e.g. not appearing).

ZPO Art. 207 Abs. 1.summary: The costs of the conciliation procedure are charged to the plaintiff if: a) the plaintiff withdraws the conciliation request; b) the procedure is discontinued due to default; or c) a permission to sue is granted.
ZPO Art. 207 Abs. 1.draft: The costs of the conciliation procedure are charged to the plaintiff if: a) the plaintiff withdraws the conciliation request; b) the procedure is discontinued due to default; or c) a permission to sue is granted.

ZPO Art. 207 Abs. 2.summary: When the action is filed in court, the conciliation costs are added to the costs of the main case.
ZPO Art. 207 Abs. 2.draft: When a lawsuit is filed, the court attaches the costs to the main case. This applies unless the court decides otherwise.
ZPO Art. 207 Abs. 2.change_note: Removed an invented exception ('unless the court decides otherwise').

ZPO Art. 208 Abs. 1.summary: If the parties reach an agreement, the conciliation authority records a settlement, a confession of claim, or an unconditional withdrawal of the claim in the minutes and has the parties sign them. Each party receives a copy of the minutes.
ZPO Art. 208 Abs. 1.draft: If the parties reach an agreement, the conciliation authority records a settlement, a confession of claim, or an unconditional withdrawal of the claim in the minutes and has the parties sign them. Each party receives a copy of the minutes.

ZPO Art. 208 Abs. 2.summary: A settlement, a confession of claim, or an unconditional withdrawal of the claim have the effect of a final and binding judgment.
ZPO Art. 208 Abs. 2.draft: A settlement, a confession of claim, or an unconditional withdrawal of the claim have the effect of a final and binding judgment.

ZPO Art. 209 Abs. 1.summary: If no agreement is reached, the conciliation authority records this in the protocol and issues the authorisation to sue: a. in the case of challenging rent or lease increases: to the landlord or lessor; b. in all other cases: to the party that filed the claim.
ZPO Art. 209 Abs. 1.draft: If no agreement is reached, the conciliation authority records this in the protocol and issues the authorisation to sue: a. in the case of challenging rent or lease increases: to the landlord or lessor; b. in all other cases: to the party that filed the claim.

ZPO Art. 209 Abs. 2.summary: The claim authorization must include: a) the names and addresses of the parties and any representatives; b) the claimant's legal request with the subject of the dispute and any counterclaim; c) the date the conciliation procedure was initiated; d) the decision on the costs of the conciliation procedure; e) the date of the claim authorization; f) the signature of the conciliation authority.
ZPO Art. 209 Abs. 2.draft: The claim authorization must include: a) the names and addresses of the parties and any representatives; b) the claimant's legal request with the subject of the dispute and any counterclaim; c) the date the conciliation procedure was initiated; d) the decision on the costs of the conciliation procedure; e) the date of the claim authorization; f) the signature of the conciliation authority.

ZPO Art. 209 Abs. 3.summary: Once notified, the authorisation to sue allows the action to be filed in court within three months.
ZPO Art. 209 Abs. 3.draft: After the conciliation authority issues the lawsuit permission, it authorizes the filing of the lawsuit with the court for a period of three months.

ZPO Art. 209 Abs. 4.summary: In disputes over the rental or lease of residential and business premises and over agricultural leases, the deadline for filing the action in court is 30 days.
ZPO Art. 209 Abs. 4.draft: In disputes arising from the lease or rent of residential and commercial spaces, as well as from agricultural lease, the claim period is 30 days.
ZPO Art. 209 Abs. 4.change_note: Clarified what the 30-day period is (deadline to file in court after the authorisation).

ZPO Art. 210 Abs. 1.summary: The conciliation authority may submit a decision proposal to the parties in: a. disputes under the Gender Equality Act of 24 March 1995; b. disputes over the rental or lease of residential and business premises and agricultural leases, where the deposit of rent, protection against abusive rents, protection against termination or extension of the lease is concerned; c. other financial disputes with a value in dispute of up to CHF 10,000.
ZPO Art. 210 Abs. 1.draft: The conciliation authority may submit a proposal for a decision in: (a) disputes under the Equality Act of March 24, 1995; (b) disputes concerning the lease and hire of residential and business premises, as well as agricultural lease, where the deposit of rent and lease payments, protection against abusive rent and lease terms, protection against termination, or the extension of the lease or hire relationship is at issue; (c) other pecuniary disputes with a value up to 10,000 Swiss francs.
ZPO Art. 210 Abs. 1.change_note: 'Abusive rent and lease terms' corrected to abusive rents.

ZPO Art. 210 Abs. 2.summary: The decision proposal may include a brief justification; otherwise, Article 238 applies by analogy.
ZPO Art. 210 Abs. 2.draft: The decision proposal may include a brief justification; otherwise, Article 238 applies by analogy.

ZPO Art. 211 Abs. 1.summary: The decision proposal is deemed accepted and has the effect of a final decision if no party rejects it within 20 days of its written notification. A rejection needs no reasons.
ZPO Art. 211 Abs. 1.draft: The decision proposal is deemed accepted and has the effects of a final decision if no party rejects it in writing within 20 days of its written communication. The rejection does not require any justification.
ZPO Art. 211 Abs. 1.change_note: Removed the added requirement that the rejection be 'in writing' (the text puts 'written' on the notification).

ZPO Art. 211 Abs. 2.summary: After receiving a rejection, the conciliation authority issues the authorisation to sue: a. in matters under Article 210 para. 1 letter b, to the party that rejected the proposal; b. in all other cases, to the claimant.
ZPO Art. 211 Abs. 2.draft: After receiving a rejection, the conciliation authority issues the statement of claim to: a. the rejecting party in matters under Article 210, paragraph 1, letter b; b. the claiming party in all other cases.
ZPO Art. 211 Abs. 2.change_note: 'Statement of claim' mistranslated Klagebewilligung (authorisation to sue).

ZPO Art. 211 Abs. 3.summary: In matters under Article 210 para. 1 letter b, if the action is not filed in time, the decision proposal is deemed accepted and has the effect of a final decision.
ZPO Art. 211 Abs. 3.draft: If a claim is not filed in time regarding matters under Article 210, paragraph 1, letter b, the settlement proposal is deemed accepted and has the effects of a final and binding decision.

ZPO Art. 211 Abs. 4.summary: The decision proposal must inform the parties of the effects set out in paragraphs 1–3.
ZPO Art. 211 Abs. 4.draft: The parties must be informed in the settlement proposal about the effects described in paragraphs 1–3.

ZPO Art. 212 Abs. 1.summary: In financial disputes with a value in dispute of up to CHF 2,000, the conciliation authority may decide the case if the claimant requests it.
ZPO Art. 212 Abs. 1.draft: The conciliation authority may decide property disputes with a value of up to 2,000 francs if the plaintiff makes a corresponding request.

ZPO Art. 212 Abs. 2.draft: The procedure is oral. This applies unless the court determines that a written procedure is appropriate.

ZPO Art. 212 Abs. 3.summary: When it decides under paragraph 1, the conciliation authority sets the court costs and the party compensation.
ZPO Art. 212 Abs. 3.draft: When the conciliation authority makes a decision under paragraph 1, it determines the court costs and the party's legal fees.

ZPO Art. 243 Abs. 1.summary: The simplified procedure applies to financial disputes with a value in dispute of up to CHF 30,000.
ZPO Art. 243 Abs. 1.draft: The simplified procedure applies to property disputes with a value of up to 30,000 Swiss francs.

ZPO Art. 243 Abs. 2.summary: Regardless of the value in dispute, the simplified procedure applies to disputes: a. under the Gender Equality Act of 24 March 1995; b. over violence, threats or stalking under Art. 28b ZGB or electronic monitoring under Art. 28c ZGB; c. over the rental or lease of residential and business premises and agricultural leases, where the deposit of rent, protection against abusive rents, protection against termination or extension of the lease is concerned; d. to enforce the right of access under Art. 25 of the Data Protection Act (DSG); e. under the Participation Act of 17 December 1993; f. over supplementary insurance to social health insurance under the Federal Health Insurance Act of 18 March 1994.
ZPO Art. 243 Abs. 2.draft: Without regard to the amount in dispute, the simplified procedure applies to disputes: a. under the Equality Act of March 24, 1995; b. concerning violence, threats, or stalking under Article 28b ZGB or electronic surveillance under Article 28c ZGB; c. regarding the lease and hire of residential and business premises as well as agricultural lease, where the deposit of rent and lease payments, protection against abusive rent and lease terms, termination protection, or the extension of the lease or hire relationship is at issue; d. to enforce the right to information under Article 25 DSG; e. under the Participation Act of December 17, 1993; f. concerning supplementary insurance to social health insurance under the Federal Act of March 18, 1994 on Health Insurance.
ZPO Art. 243 Abs. 2.change_note: 'Abusive rent and lease terms' corrected to abusive rents.

ZPO Art. 243 Abs. 3.summary: The simplified procedure does not apply in disputes before the single cantonal instance under Articles 5 and 8 or before the commercial court under Article 6.
ZPO Art. 243 Abs. 3.draft: This provision does not apply to disputes before the sole cantonal authority under Articles 5 and 8, nor to disputes before the Commercial Court under Article 6.
ZPO Art. 243 Abs. 3.change_note: 'This provision' replaced by the simplified procedure; 'authority' -> instance (a court).

ZPO Art. 257 Abs. 1.summary: The court provides legal protection through summary proceedings if: (a) the facts are undisputed or immediately provable, and (b) the legal situation is clear.
ZPO Art. 257 Abs. 1.draft: The court provides legal protection through summary proceedings if: (a) the facts are undisputed or immediately provable, and (b) the legal situation is clear.

ZPO Art. 257 Abs. 2.summary: This protection is not available if the matter is subject to the ex officio principle (Offizialgrundsatz).
ZPO Art. 257 Abs. 2.draft: This legal protection is excluded when the matter is subject to the official principle.
ZPO Art. 257 Abs. 2.change_note: 'Official principle' was not a recognisable term.

ZPO Art. 257 Abs. 3.summary: If this protection cannot be granted, the court does not consider the application (it is dismissed without a ruling on the merits).
ZPO Art. 257 Abs. 3.draft: If the court cannot grant this legal protection, it will not enter into the request.
ZPO Art. 257 Abs. 3.change_note: 'Will not enter into the request' was a literal translation of Nichteintreten.

VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 1.summary: The form for notifying rent increases and other unilateral contract changes under Art. 269d OR must contain: a. for rent increases: 1. the previous rent and the tenant's previous ancillary-cost charges; 2. the new rent and the tenant's new ancillary-cost charges; 3. the date the increase takes effect; 4. clear reasons for the increase, with a separate amount for each reason if several are given; 5. for additional services, whether the landlord receives subsidies for value-enhancing improvements; b. for other unilateral changes: 1. a description of the demand; 2. the date it takes effect; 3. clear reasons for it; c. in both cases: 1. the legal requirements for challenging it; 2. the list of conciliation authorities and their local competence.
VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 1.draft: The form for notifying rent increases and other unilateral contract changes under Article 269d OR must include: for rent increases, the previous rent and previous tenant's ancillary cost charges, the new rent and new tenant's ancillary cost charges, the effective date of the increase, a clear justification of the increase, each individual amount if multiple reasons are cited, and whether the landlord receives subsidies for value-increasing improvements; for other unilateral contract changes, a description of the change and its effective date, and a clear justification; and for both cases, the legal grounds for contesting the change and a list of conciliation authorities with their local jurisdiction.
VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 1.change_note: 'Previous tenant's' could be read as the former tenant; 'legal grounds for contesting' -> legal requirements; kept the a/b/c structure.

VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 1bis.summary: If the reasons are given in an accompanying letter, the landlord must expressly say so on the form.
VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 1bis.draft: If the establishment of a maintenance obligation occurs in an accompanying letter, the landlord must explicitly point this out on the form.
VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 1bis.change_note: Serious mistranslation: Begründung means the reasons, not 'establishment of a maintenance obligation'.

VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 2.summary: When the landlord adjusts the rent according to an agreed index, paragraphs 1 and 1bis apply by analogy. The notice of such an adjustment may not be given earlier than after the new index figure has been publicly announced.
VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 2.draft: When the landlord adjusts the rent according to an agreed index, paragraphs 1 and 1bis apply by analogy. The notice of such an adjustment may not be given earlier than after the new index figure has been publicly announced.

VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 3.summary: When cantons make the prescribed form mandatory for new rental agreements under Article 270, paragraph 2 of the Swiss Code of Obligations, paragraphs 1 and 1bis apply accordingly. The form must also include the reference interest rate and the consumer price index level that applied to the previous rent.
VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 3.draft: When cantons make the prescribed form mandatory for new rental agreements under Article 270, paragraph 2 of the Swiss Code of Obligations, paragraphs 1 and 1bis apply accordingly. The form must also include the reference interest rate and the consumer price index level that applied to the previous rent.

VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 4.summary: The cantons ensure that sufficient forms are available in the municipalities. For this purpose, they may place their own forms in the municipal offices.
VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 4.draft: The cantons ensure that sufficient forms are available in the municipalities. For this purpose, they may place their own forms in the municipal offices.

VMWG Art. 20 Abs. 1.summary: When the landlord increases the rent due to cost increases or value-enhancing improvements, the tenant can demand a numerical justification of the claimed difference. The 30-day objection period remains unaffected.
VMWG Art. 20 Abs. 1.draft: When the landlord increases the rent due to cost increases or value-enhancing improvements, the tenant can demand a numerical justification of the claimed difference. The 30-day objection period remains unaffected.

VMWG Art. 20 Abs. 2.summary: During the conciliation procedure, the tenant may demand that the landlord submit the relevant documents for every ground of the rent increase being claimed.
VMWG Art. 20 Abs. 2.draft: During the conciliation procedure, the tenant may demand that the landlord submit the relevant documents for every ground of the rent increase being claimed.

Samstagsgesetz Art. 1.summary: Regarding federal legal deadlines and deadlines set by authorities under federal law, Saturday is treated as an official public holiday.
Samstagsgesetz Art. 1.draft: Regarding federal legal deadlines and deadlines set by authorities under federal law, Saturday is treated as an official public holiday.
